title: kith-attach: BlobStore on-disk blob storage
description:
What: Implement BlobStore in the kith-attach crate — on-disk blob storage with secure id generation and path-traversal-safe access.

Algorithm:
1. Add rand = {version="0.8", features=["std"]} to kith-attach/Cargo.toml; add kith-core as dep.
2. Define BlobStore struct: { base_dir: PathBuf }.
3. BlobStore::new(base_dir: &Path) -> Self: store path; create_dir_all at startup (sync, called from main).
4. generate_blob_id() -> String: rand::Rng gen 32 bytes → format as lowercase hex (64 chars).
5. validate_blob_id(id: &str) -> Result<(), KithError>: reject empty; reject any char outside [a-zA-Z0-9_-]; reject len > 128; reject leading dot.
6. blob_path(&self, id: &str) -> PathBuf: self.base_dir.join(id). Only call after validate_blob_id.
7. write_blob(&self, id: &str, data: &[u8]) -> Result<u64, KithError>: validate_blob_id → write to {id}.tmp → sync_all → rename to {id}. Return bytes written.
8. read_blob(&self, id: &str) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, KithError>: validate_blob_id → fs::read. Return None for NotFound.
9. delete_blob(&self, id: &str) -> Result<(), KithError>: validate_blob_id → fs::remove_file. Ignore ENOENT.

Defensive rules: validate_blob_id rejects slash, dot, backslash, null, percent; write via tmp+rename for atomicity; never log blob content.

Agent team: R reads kith-core error types; I implements; T writes unit tests with known-good/bad blob ids and verify write/read/delete round-trip with sha256; V runs cargo test -p kith-attach + clippy.
